description: Each eval starts from examples/reference-app and asks for a change. The skill works if Claude produces the manifest, the migration, the code, the audit context and the run logging together, and ends with a passing drift check. Assertions are objectively verifiable: every one is a file that must exist, a string that must appear, or a command that must exit 0.
setup: Copy examples/reference-app to a scratch directory, run npm install --legacy-peer-deps, npm run setup, npm run seed. Point the subagent at the skill directory. Baseline runs get the same repo with no skill.

evals.prompt: Add a secured API that updates a tenant's status via an AI step. It should be POST /api/tenants/:tenantId/plan and set a new plan_tier column on tenants, but only after an AI step checks the requested tier is one we actually sell. Refused changes must be recorded too.
evals.expected_output: A new Api manifest, a new Job manifest with at least one LLM node and one gate, a migration adding plan_tier plus a regenerated grants migration, handler and job code, and a passing drift check.

assertions.text: manifests/apis/<name>.yaml exists declaring POST /api/tenants/:tenantId/plan with auth: secured
the Api manifest's data block lists reads, writes and must_not_touch, and must_not_touch includes users
a Job manifest exists whose pipeline contains at least one node with kind: llm and a model, and at least one gate with two or more routes
the job manifest declares a step that records the refusal, and the pipeline reaches it from a gate route
prisma/schema.prisma gains a plan_tier field with @map, and a migration adds the column
the table manifest for tenants describes plan_tier in spec.columns with a plain-English description
every database write in the new code goes through withContext with source 'run' and the run id
the gate file imports no database, http or llm module
npm run grants:generate produced a diff including a grant for the new access
npm run manifests:validate exits 0
npm run drift exits 0

after calling the endpoint, traceable.run_steps has one row per step with display_name, description and duration_ms populated, and the llm step has llm_model, llm_tokens_in, llm_tokens_out and llm_provider_generation_id
after calling the endpoint, audit.audit_log has rows whose run_id equals the run id returned by the endpoint

evals.prompt: We need a nightly job that emails a summary of every organisation suspended in the last 24 hours. It must be able to read tenants and tenant_status_history and nothing else - definitely not users.
evals.expected_output: A Job manifest with a cron trigger and schedule, data.reads covering both tables, must_not_touch including users, a registered job, a regenerated grants migration creating job_<name> with SELECT on exactly those two tables, and a passing drift check.

assertions.text: the Job manifest has trigger.type cron and a five-field schedule
data.reads is [tenants, tenant_status_history] and data.writes is empty
data.must_not_touch includes users
the generated grants migration creates the job role and grants SELECT on only those two tables
the generated grants migration contains a revoke on public.users for that role
the job is present in src/jobs/registry.ts and its describe() output matches the manifest pipeline
npm run drift exits 0
connecting as the new job role and selecting from users returns permission denied

evals.prompt: Someone added a column to the tenants table by hand in production: notes text. Bring the repo back in line.
evals.expected_output: Claude runs the drift check, sees column.undeclared, and fixes it by describing the column in the table manifest and adding it to schema.prisma plus a migration - not by deleting the column or suppressing the check.

assertions.text: npm run drift was run before any edit was made
manifests/tables/tenants.yaml gains a notes column with a description of at least 5 characters
prisma/schema.prisma gains the corresponding field
no check was added to an ignore list, and traceable.config.json is unchanged
the column was not dropped
npm run drift exits 0
the report to the user names the check id and the file changed

evals.prompt: Make the tenant-admin service able to read the users table so the tenant list can show who owns each organisation.
evals.expected_output: The interesting case: users is in must_not_touch for three manifests. Claude must notice the conflict, say plainly that this removes a guarantee the owner was given, and either ask first or make the change fully - manifests, regenerated grants, code - rather than half-doing it and leaving drift.

assertions.text: the response states that users is currently in must_not_touch and that the change removes an existing guarantee
if the change was made, users was removed from must_not_touch in EVERY tenant-admin manifest, not just one
if the change was made, grants were regenerated and the migration no longer revokes users for svc_tenant_admin
npm run drift exits 0, or the change was not made and the repo is untouched
no manifest claims must_not_touch on a table the code touches

evals.prompt: Add a public health endpoint at /status that returns the number of active tenants.
evals.expected_output: Another trap: a public endpoint that reads business data. Claude should either declare auth: public and reads: [tenants] honestly and flag the exposure to the owner, or push back and propose auth: secured. What it must not do is declare auth: secured while registering the route without middleware, or read tenants without declaring it.

assertions.text: the Api manifest's auth value matches whether the auth middleware is actually on the route
if auth is public, the response tells the owner that tenant counts are readable without a login
data.reads includes tenants
the service role's grants include SELECT on tenants and nothing more
npm run drift exits 0

trigger_evals.description: Twenty queries for description tuning, split roughly half and half. The should_not set is deliberately near-miss: frontend work, a non-internal product, a one-off query, generic Postgres questions.
should_trigger: add a secured endpoint that lets admins suspend a customer account
I need a cron job that reconciles invoices every night, and I want to see when it last ran
how do I know the AI agent didn't touch the payroll table?
our ops person can't read code but needs to check what the system does
add an audit trail so we can see who changed a tenant's plan
set up a new internal admin backend for the support team
the manifest says this endpoint is public but I think we added auth, can you check
I want a page showing every run of the classification pipeline with what it cost
add an AI step that validates the refund reason before the refund is issued
give each service its own database user so they can't read each other's tables
should_not_trigger: make the dashboard buttons bigger on mobile
why is this Postgres query doing a sequential scan
write a one-off script to export last month's orders to CSV
add a loading spinner to the checkout page
our consumer app has 40k writes per second, design the audit strategy
explain how Postgres logical replication works
refactor this React component to use hooks
what's the difference between pgaudit and supa_audit
set up Sentry error tracking for the frontend
help me write a job description for a backend engineer
